explain.say: India's Bhakra Dam and America's Grand Coulee hold back whole lakes with sheer weight: they are gravity dams. On the board, a thirty metre tall concrete gravity dam with a triangular section, water on its left. Let us see the forces battling across it.

explain.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a concrete gravity dam. Its huge weight holds back the reservoir. Look at the crest, the gallery inside, and the grout curtain sealing the rock below. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

explain.say: Look at the water push. Water pressure grows with depth: at the base it is nine point eight one times thirty, about two hundred and ninety four kilopascals. The total push is the area of that pressure triangle, half times nine point eight one times thirty squared, about four thousand four hundred kilonewtons for each metre of dam, acting ten metres up.

explain.say: The dam's weight fights back. A triangle thirty metres high and twenty four metres wide at the base, in concrete at twenty four kilonewtons per cubic metre, weighs eight thousand six hundred and forty kilonewtons per metre. Against tipping over its toe that gives a safety factor of about three point one. But see the upward arrow: water seeping under the base lifts the dam and cuts that margin.

explain.say: That is why dams have drains under them. Gravity is one of three main types. An arch dam is a thin curved shell that pushes the water load sideways into the rock walls of a narrow canyon. An embankment dam is a huge mound of earth and rock with a watertight clay core, ideal for wide valleys. Which would you pick for a wide valley with soft ground?

explain.say: Embankment! Each type fails in its own way: gravity dams by sliding or tipping, arch dams if the canyon walls give way, embankment dams by overtopping or by seepage washing out the core. That is why spillways and drains matter so much. Superb! Challenge: why is a gravity dam so much wider at the base than at the top?

faq.q: How do you calculate the water force on a dam?
faq.a: For a vertical face, the force per metre length is half times the unit weight of water times the depth squared, acting at one third of the depth above the base. For 30 metres of water that is about 4415 kilonewtons per metre.

faq.q: How does a gravity dam resist the water?
faq.a: By its own weight. The weight creates friction at the base against sliding and a restoring moment against tipping over the toe.
asks: Why are gravity dams so heavy?

faq.q: What is uplift pressure under a dam?
faq.a: Water seeping under the dam pushes up on its base, reducing its effective weight and its resistance to sliding and overturning. Drains and grout curtains are used to cut uplift.

faq.q: How does an arch dam work?
faq.a: An arch dam curves upstream, so the water pressure is carried sideways as compression into the canyon walls. It needs strong rock abutments but uses far less concrete than a gravity dam.
An embankment dam is built from compacted earth or rock fill, usually with an impervious clay core or a facing, and filters to control seepage. It suits wide valleys and weaker foundations.

facts: Water pressure rises by about 9.81 kilopascals for every metre of depth.
China's Three Gorges Dam, a concrete gravity dam, hosts the world's largest power station, about 22,500 MW.
Tarbela Dam in Pakistan is one of the largest earth- and rock-fill dams in the world by volume.
